name_or_item: Commercial Motor 10-cwt petrol van maintenance, 200 miles a week
scope: maintenance item only; a combined total of routine servicing and repairs and overhauls
source_ref: The Commercial Motor, 9 January 1959, p. 76, '10-cwt. Oilers Could Save Money'; https://archive.commercialmotor.com/article/9th-january-1959/76/10-cwt-oilers-could-save-money
notes: STATED. The oil-engined version of the same van is 0.57d. a mile. The article attributes the 0.28d difference to less frequent servicing and to two replacement petrol engines in a 100,000-mile life.

name_or_item: Commercial Motor 10-cwt oil-engined van maintenance, 200 miles a week

source_ref: The Commercial Motor, 9 January 1959, p. 76; https://archive.commercialmotor.com/article/9th-january-1959/76/10-cwt-oilers-could-save-money

name_or_item: Two replacement petrol engines per 100,000 miles, 10-cwt van
scope: engine replacement only, being the difference between the petrol and oil maintenance figures
source_ref: Computed from The Commercial Motor, 9 January 1959, p. 76
notes: DERIVED. 0.28d x 100,000 miles = GBP 116 13s 4d for two engines, GBP 58 6s 8d each; 0.28/0.85 = 33 per cent of the petrol van's maintenance total. An upper bound: the difference also covers the oil engine's less frequent servicing.
